draft.title: Houses and daily life
card: Houses in Pompeii and Herculaneum show how wealthy their owners were. The House of the Faun in Pompeii was one of the largest and richest homes in the town.
Wall paintings and mosaics

Wealthy owners decorated rooms with painted walls and floors made of tiny stone pieces. The House of the Faun held a famous floor mosaic of a battle scene. These works show the owner's money and taste.
Gardens
Large houses could have gardens with plants, fountains and statues. A garden took space and money to keep, so it was a sign of wealth.
Graffiti
Graffiti are words scratched or written on walls. Ordinary people wrote them, and they record everyday thoughts, such as jokes, insults, greetings and love messages.
draft.remember: Houses show the wealth of their owners, and graffiti show what ordinary people thought day to day.

a.q: What can historians learn from the mosaics and gardens of a house like the House of the Faun?
opts: How wealthy and fashionable the owner was
What the town's election candidates promised
How many slaves the town's baths could hold
Which gods the town's priests worshipped
a.why: Costly mosaics and large gardens needed money to make and keep, so they show the owner's wealth and taste. Election promises are not shown by house decoration, which is why the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what it costs to make and keep these features.

b.q: A historian wants to find out what ordinary people of Pompeii thought about daily matters such as friends, jokes and love. Which source is most useful?
opts: Graffiti scratched on walls
The floor mosaic of a large house
The size of a wealthy home's garden
The layout of a rich family's rooms
b.why: Graffiti were written by ordinary people and record their own thoughts. The mosaic, garden and room layout mainly show the wealth and choices of rich owners, so they say less about everyday thoughts.
b.clue: Which source was written by the people themselves?

a.best: How wealthy and fashionable the owner was

problems.detail: "Ordinary people wrote them" is too absolute. Graffiti at Pompeii and Herculaneum were written by a wide range of people, from slaves and visitors to wealthier residents. Saying many were written by ordinary people would be more accurate for HSC students, who need to weigh the reliability and authorship of sources.
